transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-10
Time: 09:30 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Kim (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (AeroNav), Tom Reyes (AeroNav), Alicia Gomez (AeroNav)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be imperfect):
- Quick review of last week's pilot numbers: average throughput up 22% with earlier batching policy, but 95th tail still above SLA during spikes.
- Discussed lowering max_concurrency and enabling adaptive batching window, plus targeted KV cache warm-up.
- Agreed next steps: Redwood to share config and trace script; AeroNav to run 95th-percentile test and share results.

Topics: throughput numbers, continuous batching tweaks, queue shaping, concurrency targets, tail latency, next steps

Transcript:
00:00 - Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, we good?
00:06 - Priya: Yep, Priya here. Sorry I stepped out earlier, had a stand-up.
00:10 - Tom: Tom on my side.
00:13 - Alicia: Alicia, all set.
00:15 - Jonah: Jonah from Redwood. I'll take the deep lane on the tuning items.
00:20 - Maya: Cool. Quick agenda: run through last week's pilot metrics, review the retuned batching policy we pushed on Friday, decide on a concurrency target for the next run, and assign tasks.
00:29 - Priya: Sounds good. We saw the average tokens/sec improvement but the 95th is... still spiky. During our 10:30am spike we hit 380 ms tails which puts us over our 300ms SLO.
00:44 - Maya: Okay that's consistent with what Jonah saw in the traces, we saw a pattern of queue buildup leading into the spike.
00:51 - Jonah: Yeah, I captured some of that. The continuous batching change reduced per-token overhead but increased the variance when bursts arrive faster than the batch drain. So batching helps throughput but can worsen tail unless you combine with queue shaping or concurrency limits.
01:10 - Tom: When you say queue shaping, do you mean applying token-level backpressure or limiting inflight requests per model shard?
01:18 - Jonah: Both are options. Practically we usually start with two levers: an inflight concurrency cap (requests per model instance) and an adaptive max_wait_ms for the batcher that shrinks under high load.
01:31 - Priya: Last run we set max_wait_ms to 12ms, batch_size to 128. Maybe we need a smaller max_wait during bursts.
01:39 - Jonah: Right — our suggestion was dynamic: max_wait_ms = base (12ms) * load_factor^-0.5 with floor at 4ms. That keeps batching at low load but tightens during surges.
01:52 - Alicia: That sounds like magic math, but is it safe for quality? We don't want hallucination risk or truncated contexts.
01:59 - Jonah: No change to model tokens or truncation. This only changes the micro-batching timing window before the runtime emits a batch for inference. The model sees the same inputs.
02:10 - Maya: Also worth noting: we can do aggressive KV-cache warming for warm traffic (prefix caching) to shave consistent tokens off the hot path.
02:20 - Priya: We have a few heavy prompt patterns at the start of sessions; warm-up could definitely help. Could you provide a script to prewarm?
02:27 - Jonah: Absolutely. I'll add a prewarm runner that replays prefixes to the model at low priority.
02:35 - Tom: Back to concurrency targets, what's the tradeoff if we reduce inflight from 32 to 16?
02:42 - Jonah: Reducing inflight reduces queuing inside the worker and lowers tail variance, but it reduces total throughput capacity per instance. If you have auto-scale set, the system will spin more workers but that increases cost. It's a cost vs tail-latency trade.
02:58 - Priya: For us cost isn't the primary limiter during pilot; tail latency is. We need to see stable 95th below 300ms before we move to production.
03:09 - Maya: Good, then we prioritize tail. Proposal: next run set inflight concurrency to 16, enable adaptive max_wait_ms with floor 4ms, keep batch_size at 128, and enable KV prewarm for top 20 prompts.
03:24 - Tom: Can we keep a 2-min warmup window so that autoscaler doesn't consider us cold?
03:30 - Jonah: Yes, set min_idle_workers and keep-alive accordingly. We'll include recommended autoscale playbook entries.
03:36 - Priya: On Friday's traces, there are a few spikes where CPU on the worker node shot up and we saw 1-2 requeues. Any idea what caused that?
03:45 - Jonah: Some of those were background GC and S3 fetch delays for larger embeddings. I'm patching the fetch path to make it async and not block the batching thread. There was also one case where a long-running request held the token mutex because of a callout to a remote tool.
03:58 - Tom: Are tool calls part of our request path? We did enable a plugin that does entity enrichment, and that might be slowing things.
04:05 - Priya: We do entity enrichment for certain endpoints. It may be hitting an external REST call. We can try caching enrichment results.
04:13 - Alicia: Can we route tool calls to a separate worker pool so they don't block critical inference threads?
04:18 - Jonah: Yep, that's a great pattern. Redwood supports policy-based routing: route requests that need tool calls to a different pool with higher timeout and lower concurrency. We'll draft a routing policy for you.
04:30 - Maya: Let's capture decisions: reduce inflight to 16, adaptive max_wait_ms floor 4ms, KV prewarm top-20 prefixes, route tool-call requests to dedicated pool, and recommend autoscale/keep-alive.
04:44 - Priya: Quick question on observability — the traces you provided show token-level timing, but we don't have a mapping to our client-side timestamp. Can we get a script to merge client and server times?
04:56 - Jonah: Yes, Jonah: I'll provide a small wrapper that attaches client ts and correlates with server spans. That will help debug whether it's network jitter or server-side queueing.
05:06 - Tom: Also would be useful to capture queue depth metrics per worker over the run window, can Redwood emit that?
05:12 - Jonah: We can add a metric export; we already emit internal queue_length gauge. We'll make sure it's included in the dashboard and the CSV export so you can plot percentiles.
05:23 - Priya: One more operational ask — do you have a recommended replay batch size for our synthetic 5k request test? We want it to mimic production mix: 60% short prompts, 30% medium, 10% long.
05:35 - Maya: For that mix, suggest peak concurrency ramp to 400 qps for 2 minutes, then hold 120 qps steady for 10 minutes. We'll supply the script with distribution.
05:47 - Priya: Great.
05:49 - Jonah: On the batching policy nuance — we also added a token budget per batch so really large requests don't occupy the whole batch. We set token_budget_per_batch = 4096 in dev. That prevents single long inputs from starving others.
06:05 - Alicia: Oh that might explain some of our long tails; we have a small subset of requests with long contexts.
06:11 - Tom: Can we add a per-route override so those long-context endpoints have a larger token budget?
06:16 - Jonah: Yep, per-route overrides are supported. We'll include a suggested config: routeA token_budget 8192, routeB keep default.
06:25 - Maya: Okay, any concerns with the proposed plan?
06:28 - Priya: Not from our side. We want to ensure the next run captures tail metrics and trace merging.
06:35 - Alicia: Also add an SLO dashboard tile for 95th latency and queue depth.
06:40 - Jonah: Noted. I'll add dashboard widgets and the CSV export.
06:44 - Maya: Timing for deliverables? Jonah and I will push configs and scripts by EOD Friday (which is 2026-11-13). Priya you'll run the 5k test and get us logs by 2026-11-16. Then we meet week of 2026-11-17 to pick final concurrency target.
07:02 - Priya: Yes that works.
07:05 - Tom: One more question: fallback policies — if we still hit tails under full load, what's your suggestion?
07:12 - Jonah: We have two fallback levers: transparently fallback to a lower-cost, lower-latency model variant (smaller quantized checkpoint) for non-critical routes, or enable partial responses/early-exit for internal endpoints. For customer-facing SLO-sensitive routes, prefer model variant fallback with warnings.
07:30 - Alicia: For regulatory reasons, we prefer not to change model fidelity for certain routes. Those will be pinned and require autoscale sizing.
07:38 - Maya: We'll annotate those pinned routes in the routing policy.
07:41 - Priya: Regarding cost: do you have a rough estimate of extra nodes we might need if we drop inflight from 32 to 16 to maintain throughput?
07:49 - Jonah: Rough back-of-envelope: doubling worker count if traffic profile remains unchanged. But with batching tuning and prewarm, we expect partial recovery, so maybe +30% nodes. We'll put a cost estimate in the follow-up email.
08:05 - Tom: Perfect.
08:08 - Maya: Ok, quick recap and owners:
08:11 - Maya: Jonah — provide: 1) tuned batching config, 2) KV prewarm runner, 3) trace merge script, 4) dashboard widget additions, all by 2026-11-13.
08:24 - Jonah: Got it.
08:26 - Priya: Priya — run the synthetic 5k test and upload logs by 2026-11-16.
08:33 - Priya: Yup.
08:34 - Tom: Tom will sanity check tool-call routing and our enrichment cache.
08:40 - Tom: I'll do that and share notes by 2026-11-15.
08:44 - Alicia: I'll flag pinned routes for the routing policy and share the list.
08:49 - Alicia: Done, will be in the drive by 2026-11-12.
08:53 - Maya: Anything else?
08:55 - Priya: One tiny ask — can you include a sample Grafana panel JSON so our infra team can import?
09:00 - Jonah: Yes, we'll include an example panel JSON in the assets.
09:04 - Maya: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts.
09:08 - Priya: Thanks all.
09:10 - Tom: Thanks.
09:11 - Maya: End.
